cosy-lesson.title: Do Raindrops Select the Place Where to Fall?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Speculate – to form a theory or conjecture about a subject without firm evidence.

p.em: Example: Scientists continue to speculate about the existence of life on other planets.

cosy-blockquote.p: Trajectory – the path followed by a projectile flying or an object moving under the action of given forces.

p.em: Example: The trajectory of the raindrop was altered by a sudden gust of wind.

cosy-blockquote.p: Premeditated – planned or thought out beforehand.

p.em: Example: It is fascinating to imagine that natural processes could be premeditated rather than accidental.

cosy-blockquote.p: Haphazard – lacking any obvious principle of organization.

p.em: Example: The rain fell in a haphazard manner across the dry fields.

cosy-blockquote.p: Desolate – empty, bleak, and devoid of life.

p.em: Example: Drops falling on a desolate desert are a rare and precious occurrence.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sentient – able to perceive or feel things.

p.em: Example: Some philosophers speculate whether nature itself is sentient and purposeful.

cosy-blockquote.p: Coincidence – a remarkable concurrence of events or circumstances without apparent causal connection.

p.em: Example: It was a beautiful coincidence that the storm began just as we arrived.

cosy-blockquote.p: Heatwave – a prolonged period of abnormally hot weather.

p.em: Example: During the intense heatwave, we prayed for a single raindrop to fall.

cosy-blockquote.p: Condensation – the conversion of a vapor or gas to a liquid.

p.em: Example: Rain is formed through the natural process of condensation in clouds.

cosy-blockquote.p: Manifest – to show or demonstrate clearly.

p.em: Example: The laws of physics manifest themselves in the intricate shapes of snowflakes.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
Why do humans love to speculate about absurd or poetic questions in their daily columns?
★ What is the most unusual speculative theory you have ever pondered?

How does observing the trajectory of a single falling raindrop affect your perception of time?
★ Do you prefer standing in the rain or seeking immediate shelter during a storm?

If the natural patterns of rainfall were completely premeditated by some planetary system, how would that alter our relationship with nature?
★ Do you tend to believe that natural occurrences have a hidden meaning?

Is weather fundamentally haphazard, or is our science simply not advanced enough to see the deep structure of wind and water?
★ Are you a spontaneous person, or do you need everything to have a clear structure?

Why does rain falling upon a dry, desolate landscape feel more profound than rain falling in a crowded city?
★ Where is your favorite natural escape when you need to clear your head?

Do you believe it is possible that some organic, non-human elements of the Earth are actually sentient?
★ Have you ever felt a deep, unspoken connection to an old tree or a natural landscape?

Can a perfect rainfall precisely when a farmer needs it be a mere coincidence?
★ What is the luckiest coincidence that has ever happened to you?

If a severe heatwave grips a region, could the atmosphere be choosing to redirect rain to cool down the hottest places on Earth?
★ How do you cope physically and mentally during extreme summer heatwaves?

How does the simple chemistry of condensation turn into a highly emotional weather event for poets and artists?
★ Is there a particular song or piece of art that perfectly captures the feeling of rain for you?

In what ways do environmental laws and patterns manifest themselves in our daily psychological states?
★ Does the weather have a direct, noticeable impact on your daily motivation levels?

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
Modern columns encourage us to speculate on poetic questions, whereas our ancestors focused their thoughts on concrete, daily survival.
★ What is the most unusual speculative theory you have ever pondered?

Algorithms try to map every trajectory in our lives, killing the beautiful, random detours that older generations regularly experienced.
★ When was the last time you went for a walk without looking at a map or your phone?

We want our modern careers and schedules to be completely premeditated, while older societies surrendered their future to fate and destiny.
★ Do you find having too many choices in life liberating or completely overwhelming?

Older generations accepted the haphazard delays of life with patience, whereas modern humans demand instant, predictable gratification.
★ How do you cope when a sudden delay completely disrupts your daily plans?

Ancient people found spiritual meaning in a desolate landscape, while modern urban environments have isolated us from the rhythms of the earth.
★ Where is your favorite natural escape when you need to clear your head?

In past eras, we viewed nature as a sentient entity; today, modern rationalism treats the planet as a mere repository of raw resources.
★ Have you ever felt a deep, unspoken connection to an old tree or a natural landscape?

Our ancestors viewed a perfectly timed rainfall as a divine miracle, whereas modern meteorology dismisses it as a mere coincidence.
★ What is the luckiest coincidence that has ever happened to you?

A severe summer heatwave today is analyzed as a systemic climate crisis, whereas ancient cultures saw it as a temporary trial from the gods.
★ How do you cope physically and mentally during extreme summer heatwaves?

The simple chemistry of condensation has replaced the ancient, poetic magic that made storms feel like active, moral events.
★ Is there a particular song or piece of art that perfectly captures the feeling of rain for you?

We have conquered many physical natural laws, yet our internal psychological states are more fragmented and anxious than in past eras, a contrast that continues to manifest.
★ Does the weather have a direct, noticeable impact on your daily motivation levels?
